reviews.review: Plays like Snipper Elite 5 so I like it so far

It's ok, but the premium price for game quality is unacceptable. This game should be about $20-$30 dollars max.  I regret buying it significantly. Battlefield 1 and even the ancient game Saboteur are far better games. As others have said, it feels like DLC and blatant rehashing of the same assets and mechanics (I played Sniper Elite 3 but not 4 or 5). The story is generic and superficially executed. The characters are flat and empty as is the voice acting. The phony French and German accents are especially irritating. 

The map and level design is mediocre.  The physicality of collisions with character controller movement is terrible; sometimes you can vault over sandbags, sometimes you can't; sometimes you can drop off a ledge or over a railing, sometimes you can't. None of the maps feel like real sites, but instead game-world levels. The lighting and illumination feels like it's from the mid 2000's, and is especially poor compared to something like Battlefield 1, the Last of Us or most high-priced modern games. The navigable areas feel highly restrictive (most likely to ensure that AI can move and access the areas) but are still confusingly janky and poorly designed. You will encounter many invisible walls in areas that look walkable (even in the middle of the map) or wide gaps that look like you can walk between something like a truck and a wall but no, you can't walk there. I had one of my grenades stick to an invisible wall 3 feet in front of me.  Harry Hawker might be posing on a roof ready to snipe in the cover image, but you will never be on a roof like that.  This game feels like it should be a sandbox of creativity for getting kills and accomplishing missions, but it always feels the same.  None of your decisions will actually mean anything or do anything to change any outcome.  

If the game designers want to take Sniper Elite to the next level, they might need to look to other stories and media for inspiration. Imagine if they took inspiration from Inglorious Basterds, The Pianist, a Soldier of Orange, Operation Valkyrie or Saving Private Ryan. There are no stakes in this game, there are no people, just cartoons. There's no reason to care and thus no meaning. Once you've done 10 headshots and grenade or mine kills, you've done them all.
